> To learn how to create and set up a bot, please consult our [**Introduction to Bots**](https://core.telegram.org/bots) and [**Bot FAQ**](https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq).

* Added the method [sendWidget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendwidget), allowing bots to send messages with HTML widgets. * Added the method [sendSharedWidget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendsharedwidget), allowing bots to send again shared widgets created by the bot.
* Added the class [WidgetQuery](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#widgetquery) and the field *widget\_query* to the class [Update](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#update) for queries sent to the bot by widgets in messages sent by the bot or via the bot.

### Authorizing your bot

Each bot is given a unique authentication token [when it is created](https://core.telegram.org/bots/features#botfather). The token looks something like `123456:ABC-DEF1234ghIkl-zyx57W2v1u123ew11`, but we'll use simply **<token>** in this document instead. You can learn about obtaining tokens and generating new ones in [this document](https://core.telegram.org/bots/features#botfather).

### Making requests

All queries to the Telegram Bot API must be served over HTTPS and need to be presented in this form: `https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD_NAME`. Like this for example:

```
https://api.telegram.org/bot123456:ABC-DEF1234ghIkl-zyx57W2v1u123ew11/getMe
```

We support **GET** and **POST** HTTP methods. We support four ways of passing parameters in Bot API requests:

* [URL query string](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Query_string)
* application/x-www-form-urlencoded
* application/json (except for uploading files)
* multipart/form-data (use to upload files)

The response contains a JSON object, which always has a Boolean field 'ok' and may have an optional String field 'description' with a human-readable description of the result. If 'ok' equals *True*, the request was successful and the result of the query can be found in the 'result' field. In case of an unsuccessful request, 'ok' equals *False* and the error is explained in the 'description'. An Integer 'error\_code' field is also returned, but its contents are subject to change in the future. Some errors may also have an optional field 'parameters' of the type [ResponseParameters](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#responseparameters), which can help to automatically handle the error.

* All methods in the Bot API are case-insensitive.
* All queries must be made using UTF-8.

#### Making requests when getting updates

If you're using [**webhooks**](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#getting-updates), you can perform a request to the Bot API while sending an answer to the webhook. Use either *application/json* or *application/x-www-form-urlencoded* or *multipart/form-data* response content type for passing parameters. Specify the method to be invoked in the *method* parameter of the request. It's not possible to know that such a request was successful or get its result.

> Please see our [FAQ](https://core.telegram.org/bots/faq#how-can-i-make-requests-in-response-to-updates) for examples.

### Using a Local Bot API Server

The Bot API server source code is available at [telegram-bot-api](https://github.com/tdlib/telegram-bot-api). You can run it locally and send the requests to your own server instead of `https://api.telegram.org`. If you switch to a local Bot API server, your bot will be able to:

* Download files without a size limit.
* Upload files up to 2000 MB.

A widget is one self-contained HTML document with inline CSS and JavaScript, at most 32 KB of HTML and 4 KB after compression. Telegram apps run it on the user's device in a sandbox with **no network access at all**, draw it in the style of the chat, and keep it running while it is on screen: a poll whose bars move as people vote, a price ticker, a board game for two in a group, a promo code that copies on a tap. A widget is **fixed code plus changeable state**. The code, its HTML, is set when the widget is sent and never changes. What changes is the widget's state, and only the bot writes it: the **chat state**, tied to one message and seen only in that chat, and the **shared state**, seen wherever the widget is shown. The widget reads its state and redraws when it changes. It cannot change the state itself, but it can ask the bot with small requests, the way a callback button does. Widgets live in the private chat with the bot, in groups, in messages sent via the bot in inline mode, and in forwards to any chat. Currently, in the production environment, widgets work only in the private chat with the bot. The rest works on the [test server](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#availability). A widget can also be a **shared widget**: one widget on the server, like a poll, that any number of messages show, with one shared state for all of them. This page is a guide to designing and implementing widgets, followed by the reference of the widget's JavaScript object `TelegramWidget`. **Where a widget may ask** is decided by the server for each message, from the widget's flags (a static widget's message, or the shared widget), and passed to the widget by the app:

| Message | On a tap | In the background | `viewer` | `chatType` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the original in the private chat with the bot | Yes | Yes | the user | `'private'` |
| an original in a group | Yes | No | the user | `'group'`, `'supergroup'` |
| an original sent via the bot | Yes | No | the user | the chat's type |
| a forward of a shared widget | Yes | No | the user | `null` |
| a forward of a static widget | No | No | `null` | `null` |

This is for a widget sent with `allow_queries`. A widget without it asks nowhere, its originals included, and has no `viewer`. Elsewhere `request()` rejects with `NOT_ALLOWED`.

**Background requests.** Only the original in the private chat with the bot may ask without a tap, and only while it is visible: one request when the widget appears on screen (scrolled into view, the app back in front), then at most one every 5 seconds while it stays visible. Apps create a widget before they show it, so a request the script makes in its first lines waits and goes out as soon as the widget appears. Ask for fresh state right at the start. Use background requests to refresh what this user sees while the chat is open. For what is the same for everyone, a [shared widget](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#static-and-shared-widgets)'s shared state needs no requests at all. Neither the server nor the bot can tell a background request from a tap.

**In the bot.** A request from an original arrives in the field `widget_query` of [Update](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#update), and one from a forwarded copy of a shared widget in the field `shared_widget_query`. If you pass `allowed_updates`, include both. Their fields depend on where the user tapped:

| Field | Original (private chat or group) | Original sent via the bot | Forward of a shared widget |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| update | `widget_query` | `widget_query` | `shared_widget_query` |
| `id`, `from`, `data` | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `chat`, `message_id` | Yes | No | No |
| `inline_message_id` | No | Yes | No |
| `chat_instance` | Yes | Yes, the chat of the tap | No |
| `chat_type` | No, see `chat.type` | Yes, the chat of the tap | No |
| `widget_id` | for a shared widget | for a shared widget | always |

  "update_id": 100000001,
  "widget_query": {
    "id": "8123456789012345678",
    "from": { "id": 111111111, "is_bot": false, "first_name": "Alice", "language_code": "en" },
    "chat": { "id": 111111111, "type": "private", "first_name": "Alice" },
    "message_id": 4242,
    "chat_instance": "901234567890123456",
    "widget_id": "7770011223344556677",

The query does not carry the widget's state: keep the authoritative state on your side, keyed by the message (or by `widget_id`), and check every request against it.

**Answering.** Call [answerWidgetQuery](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#answerwidgetquery) for **every** query, with or without `data`, within 15 seconds. Otherwise the widget's promise rejects with `TIMEOUT`. `data` is the only thing an answer carries: no change of state, no notification, no alert, no URL. The app shows nothing for an answer, and the widget shows the result itself.

```
POST https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/answerWidgetQuery
{ "widget_query_id": "8123456789012345678", "data": "{\"p\":5.47}" }
```

* **The answer does not change the state.** To change the chat state or the shared state, call the [methods that change it](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets#changing-the-state), before or after answering. The widget gets `chatDataChanged` / `publicDataChanged` when the new state arrives, which can be before or after the answer. A widget that needs the new state at once (the user's own vote, the new board) gets it from the bot in the answer.
* **Answer also when something failed**, with a short text the widget can show: an unanswered request ends in the widget as `TIMEOUT`.

{ "chat_id": -1001234567890, "message_id": 77, "chat_data": "{\"b\":\"x---o----\",\"t\":\"x\"}" }

* **Commit after the edit.** Put a user's move into your own state only once the edit went through, so a failed edit does not take a turn away.
* **Rate limits.** An `editMessageWidgetData` call counts as one sent message against your bot's limits for sending messages. A shared widget takes at most one edit per second. Above them the method fails with a flood wait. When many users act at once (votes), coalesce your edits: keep the state on your side and write it at most once a second.

* `editSharedWidgetData` is the only way to set a shared widget's refresh period (`cache_time`).

На **10 ноября 2026** последняя версия — [**Bot API 10.4**, выпущенная 9 ноября](https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#november-9-2026). Главная новинка — **HTML-виджеты прямо внутри сообщений**: HTML, CSS и JavaScript с интерактивными кнопками. Сейчас в production они работают **только в личке с ботом**, без пересылки; группы и inline доступны на тестовом сервере. Также расширены ephemeral-ответы и поддержка TON-кошельков. Минимальный пример для **aiogram 3** — виджет со счётчиком. Метод описан через `TelegramMethod`, поэтому пример не зависит от наличия готового `send_widget` в вашей версии библиотеки. ```python import asyncio import os from aiogram import Bot, Dispatcher, F from aiogram.filters import Command from aiogram.methods.base import TelegramMethod from aiogram.types import Message class SendWidget(TelegramMethod[Message]): __api_method__ = "sendWidget" __returning__ = Message chat_id: int html: str caption: str HTML = """

Мой первый виджет

Нажатий: 0

""" dp = Dispatcher() @dp.message(Command("widget"), F.chat.type == "private") async def show_widget(message: Message, bot: Bot): await bot(SendWidget( chat_id=message.chat.id, html=HTML, caption="Интерактивный счётчик", )) async def main(): bot = Bot(token=os.environ["BOT_TOKEN"]) await dp.start_polling(bot) if __name__ == "__main__": asyncio.run(main()) ``` Установите aiogram 3, задайте `BOT_TOKEN` и отправьте `/widget` боту в личке с актуального клиента Telegram. Счётчик здесь локальный: при пересоздании виджета он сбросится. Для сохранения состояния бот использует `chat_data` и `editMessageWidgetData`; запросы из виджета идут через `TelegramWidget.request()` → `widget_query` → `answerWidgetQuery`. По [документации виджетов](https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets), внешняя сеть недоступна, а HTML ограничен **32 КБ и 4 КБ после сжатия zlib**.
